# 1 Enoch Chapter 87 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of Dreams — Animal Apocalypse

---

**87:1** And I saw one of those four white figures, that it came forth from that place and three were with it.

**87:2** And those three that had last come forth grasped me by my hand and took me up, away from the generations of the earth, and raised me up to a lofty place, and showed me a tower raised high above the earth, and all the hills were lower.

**87:3** And one said to me: "Remain here until you see everything that befalls those elephants, camels, and asses, and the stars and the oxen, and all of them."

**87:4** And I saw one of those four white figures, how he seized that first star which had fallen from heaven, and bound it hand and foot and cast it into an abyss; now that abyss was narrow and deep and horrible and dark.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering adjudicated from EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA.*

**ANIMAL APOCALYPSE — SYMBOLISM KEY (Chapter 87):**
- **Four white figures** = the four archangels (Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, Phanuel/Suryal; cf. 1 En 9:1; 40:9)
- **Enoch lifted up** (v. 2) = his visionary ascent — he becomes the observer of all subsequent history
- **Tower raised high** (v. 2) = the heavenly vantage point from which Enoch will watch the Animal Apocalypse unfold
- **First star bound and cast into abyss** (v. 4) = Semyaza (leader of the Watchers) imprisoned (cf. 1 En 10:11-13)
- **The abyss** = the place of punishment for fallen angels, described as narrow, deep, horrible, dark

*The chapter bridges the Watcher episode to the flood narrative in chapter 88.*
